items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to meetings of the board of regents
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S1796

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
meetings of the board of regents

PURPOSE:

To require the Board the Regents to hold its meetings throughout the
regions of New York State.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Section 204 of the Education Law to require the Board
of Regents to hold at least one meeting in each calendar year in each
Judicial District outside of New York City and at least one meeting in
each calendar year in New York City.

Section 2 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

New York State Law does not specify where the Board of Regents shall
hold its meetings. Therefore, the vast majority of its meetings are
held in Albany, inside the New York State Department of Education
Building. This pattern of almost always meeting in the same city, in
the same part of the state, prevents nearly the entire public from
attending and participating in the meetings of the Board of Regents.

This bill will address that issue and will encourage greater public
awareness and involvement in New York State education policy. This
legislation requires the Board of Regents to hold its meetings
throughout the regions of New York State. Specifically, it requires
that at least one meeting in each calendar year be held in each
Judicial District outside of New York City and that at least one
meeting in each calendar be held in New York City.

By requiring the Board of Regents to hold its meeting throughout all
the regions of New York State, the public, especially those affected
by the State's education policy, will have an opportunity to attend
and participate in the meetings of the Board of Regents. Instead of
being left out of the process and having to travel many hours back and
forth to Albany, under this legislation the public will be able to
have direct access to and be a part of the meetings of the Board of
Regents held in their part of the State. This will facilitate greater
dialogue between the Board of Regents and the people of the state who
reside in each judicial district.

This legislation is necessary because the adoption and implementation
of the Common Core Curriculum by the Board of Regents provides a clear
example of how the public was not well informed of the Board of
Regents' actions that have a significant impact on the schools,
teachers and students in New York State. By requiring the Board of
Regents to hold open public meetings throughout the regions of the
State, stakeholders will have an opportunity to meet with the Regents
and learn about the role the Regents play in setting education policy
for the State.


LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2013-2014: S.6856

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.  Effective immediately, the
addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary
for the implementation of this act on its effective date is authorized
to be made on or before such date.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to providing a live webcast for meetings of the board of regents
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S1796A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
providing a live webcast for meetings of the board of regents

PURPOSE:  To require that each meeting of the Board of Regents be
streamed live and be made available to the public.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new section 204-a to the education law to require
that the entirety of each meeting of the regents be live webcast and
made available on the State Education Department's (SED) website. SED
would be required to archive each meeting for no less than two years.
The Department shall notify each school district superintendent of the
upcoming regents meeting and provide information on the availability
of and where to obtain the live webcast.

Section 2 is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  Currently, the Board of Regents webcasts only a small
portion of its monthly meetings According to the Department's website,
the Regents were scheduled to publicly convene for roughly 9 hours for
their April 13th-14th, 2015 meetings. However, the Board only webcast
and archived about one hour and ten minutes of the proceedings. While
the meetings are open to the public, the Board meets primarily at the
state education building. Many concerned parents and educators are
unable to make the trip to Albany to attend. This bill would give them
the ability to stay informed of the Board's decisions regarding
educating our children.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  2014: A9547/S6856 Referred to Education

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after
it shall have become a law.
